event.summary: Check whether timeout cleanup can race a still-running provider mutation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. SPEC_impl.md, Disposable environments / Podman places, creation and images, places run/start in independent systemd scopes. Suggested bucket: other (test tooling cleanup); could-be-highest: no established route, only owned test resources implicated. Confidence: unresolved lead; proposed_drop: false; possible_cover: none. Next source checks: trace HelmProcess::stop_and_reap, provider shell command cancellation, and image commit/build timing. Exact missing premise: whether any in-flight command can create a resource after cleanup's last label query. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Fallback cleanup does not settle provider commands before certifying absence
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: a failed real Podman acceptance run can report successful fallback cleanup while a container-creation command from that same run is still running and creates an owned container afterward. These are test-owned resources, but they can remain running and consume the shared machine until explicitly cleaned. Suggested bucket: other (maintainer test cleanup); confidence: confirmed by source lifetime analysis, not observed execution; proposed_drop: false; possible_cover: none; could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route.

The timeout/panic wrapper drops exercise and calls cleanup (podman_environments.rs:1275-1300). cleanup first calls HelmProcess::stop_and_reap, then immediately inventories currently visible containers/images and declares success when those queries are empty (1198-1251). stop_and_reap only start_kill/waits the helm child (harness.rs:971-977); it neither joins nor ends provider subprocesses. Provider starts are separate systemd scopes (environment/podman.rs:295-320,417-456), and provider commands are spawned in an isolated process group (environment/podman_probe.rs:174-205). Killing the helm does not run its Rust kill-on-drop destructors or wait those children. An already-spawned command delayed before resource creation can therefore execute after the empty inventory. The cleanup loop even stops its image passes on the first empty result; no pending-send record or command completion boundary is consulted. A failure early in image preparation makes this route relevant; it does not require touching another test's resources.

The production recovery contract explicitly retains absent pending names because a disconnected command may still create them: environment/podman/build.rs:630-663 and SPEC_impl.md, Shared recipes and prepared artifacts / recipe deletion, require active work to finish its current command before ownership is forgotten. The fallback bypasses that boundary. Prefer canceling and awaiting owned build/launch work through the helm before forcibly stopping it, or retain and settle the run's exact pending commands/names before declaring fallback cleanup complete. Caveat: no frequency or exact scheduler delay was measured, and image-commit/container-removal serialization was not relied on; the established route is a pending create becoming visible only after the absence scan. No runtime tests or reproductions were run.

event.summary: Unverified after investigation: fallback cleanup may race a surviving provider create
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: fallback cleanup has no completion boundary for already-sent provider commands, so a failed real Podman test may leave a resource that becomes visible after its final empty inventory. The original consequence remains owned test resources left running or consuming storage on the shared machine; there is no established security or user-work-loss route. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence revised from confirmed to unverified after investigation: the previous event established missing synchronization but overstated the specific late-publication outcome as proven. proposed_drop: false; possible_cover: none; could-be-highest: no.

Checks and actual results: (1) podman_environments.rs:1276-1289 bounds and catches panics only in the test's exercise future. Leaving that block drops the HTTP client work; it does not cancel the server launch. sessions/sandbox.rs:61-80 starts admission through run_owned, whose lib.rs:2721-2727 tokio::spawn is detached from client cancellation, and provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:464-487 stores a separately spawned launch task. Thus a test-side timeout can reach cleanup while a real launch/prepare command is active. (2) cleanup:1198-1201 calls HelmProcess::stop_and_reap; harness.rs:971-977 calls start_kill and waits only the direct helm PID. Its spawn:1014-1027 provides no child/process-group reaper. (3) SystemPlaceCommands::execute (podman_probe.rs:178-200) spawns the local shell or SSH client in its own process group with kill_on_drop; access.rs:67-94 and 173-185 supply no parent-death signal or descendant-wait facility. backend.rs:1979-2019 calls terminate_child on handled capture timeout/output failure; terminate_child:2268-2278 kills and reaps that group. Those paths require the helm to be alive; SIGKILL does not execute Rust drop or async termination. This supports a surviving already-spawned local/SSH command, rather than a not-yet-spawned Rust task continuing after helm death. (4) helper/build.rs:554-565 persists its pending name and timestamp before sending run; reconcile_helpers:630-675 retains recent absent names. Podman scopes deliberately move run/start out of the helm/login lifetime (podman.rs:295-320). (5) fallback cleanup only lists current recipe-labelled objects at 1217-1251; it neither reads pending names nor waits the command/scope. Ordinary provider cleanup's stronger behavior does not repair that test fallback.

Exact missing premise: an actual supported Podman/systemd/local-or-SSH execution path in which the already-spawned command remains live after helm death AND completes resource publication after fallback's final empty inventory, despite pipe closure and Podman's storage/creation locks. The app source proves neither that these locks serialize inventories behind creation nor that they permit them to overtake it. A hypothetical arbitrary scheduler pause before create is not sufficient evidence of the actual failure route. The in-repo failure model represents lost replies and pending ownership but does not validate real engine publication/lock timing. Image commit may also hold container locks that force fallback rm to wait, so no commit race is claimed as confirmed. Available app-source checks settle the cancellation/process ownership and pending-name premises but cannot settle the external engine's lock/publication/pipe behavior across the supported version range. Evidence needed: primary engine/systemd/SSH source establishing such an execution path for a supported version, or an explicitly authorized controlled failure test showing command PID/scope lifetime and inventory/publication order. No runtime tests or reproductions were performed.

event.summary: Unverified after investigation: fallback cleanup lacks a provider-command completion boundary
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR and original consequence retained: a failed real Podman test may leave a resource published after fallback's final empty inventory, consuming owned test storage/processes on the shared machine. The app-source missing join is established; a real late-publication incident is not established.

This turn pursued accessible primary upstream source rather than treating external engine behavior as unavailable. With this provider's --quiet scope, that is a real pre-Podman asynchronous boundary, not evidence that a Rust task can continue after SIGKILL. Podman v4.9.3 libpod/runtime_ctr.go, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/libpod/runtime_ctr.go :414-424 performs storage setup before :530-543 registers the container in libpod state; :1159-1185 inventories registered state. Its Bolt implementation, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/libpod/boltdb_state.go :895-911, reads the current database in a transaction. Thus app-level inventory is not intrinsically a completion receipt for a not-yet-registered create. These checks supply useful concrete wait/publication boundaries but do not alone prove their ordering against this exact fixture's timeout and fallback.

Prior useful app checks remain: exercise's 30-minute timeout drops test HTTP work, while sessions/sandbox.rs:61-80 and provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:464-487 retain separate server tasks. Exact remaining premise: a supported real local/localhost-SSH command surviving helm termination that publishes after ALL fallback container/image checks, under this fixture's actual 30-minute timeout or panic route. The upstream split permits concurrency, but no checked source sequence yet proves (a) a relevant pending create at that deadline, (b) image removal not preventing it or reporting in-use instead of cleanup success, and (c) no pipe/signal termination before publication. Storage setup can precede registration, but storage/image-reference locks and fallback image removal can alter the outcome; no arbitrary scheduler pause is counted as confirmation. Systemd and Podman checks above do not settle that full composition. Evidence needed is a primary-source trace through the selected engine storage backend plus the fixture's reachable failure boundary, or an explicitly authorized controlled failure observation of command/scope, inventories and publication. No installed process was inspected, no runtime tests/reproductions performed, no claim that a resource actually leaked. event.summary: SSH bootstrap failure can leave a storage-only builder outside fallback cleanup
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. Original consequence retained and narrowed: fallback can report successful cleanup while an owned builder from the real SSH acceptance remains in Podman storage and can later become a running container. This consumes only this test's resources; no security or user-work-loss route is established. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence revised to likely, naming the external occurrence premise: a first-bootstrap remote Podman create stalls in a pre-libpod-registration filesystem operation past the 120-second command deadline and the fallback scans, while unrelated inventory reads remain usable. The conditional source route is now traced; no such storage stall or leaked process was observed. proposed_drop: false; possible_cover: none; could-be-highest: no.

Useful storage checks refute the earlier broad implication that any missed derived-image create can pass fallback: Podman 4.9.3 pins containers/storage v1.51.0 and common v0.57.4 (go.mod:13,20). store.go:1744-1758 locks layers/images while CreateContainer resolves its source; :1871-1889 records the storage container and its ImageID before releasing those locks. DeleteImage uses writeToAllStores (:1349-1372), then :2551-2560 refuses an image referenced by ANY storage container, including one not yet registered in libpod. Thus a derived-image create either loses its source image before storage creation, or protects that image and makes the fallback's final image-empty check fail. Podman's container_commit.go:42-49 holds the container lock across Commit at :169; ordinary removeContainer takes that lock, so the claimed late-commit shortcut is not established. These narrower refutations preserve the original consequence but remove those proposed routes.

The remaining source-conditional route uses the first bootstrap builder, whose source is deliberately NOT swept: podman/build.rs:41-45 runs it from cached UBUNTU, before any test-owned image exists. Podman runtime_ctr.go:442-455 completes storage setup, then calls os.MkdirAll for the container secrets directory before libpod state.AddContainer at :566-578. This filesystem boundary is outside CreateContainer's image/layer locks. Podman storage.go:123-129 creates the storage container; common inventory ps.GetContainerLists uses runtime.GetContainers at pkg/ps/ps.go:64 and adds storage-only external containers only when options.External at :89. The fixture's owned_ids command does not pass --external. Therefore during a successful-but-stalled pre-registration mkdir, normal container ls cannot see the builder. The Ubuntu base is unlabelled/user-owned for this test and intentionally retained, so no test-owned image removal supplies the otherwise protective image-use check.

Failure/child-lifetime sequence: this fixture's SSH route is ordinary non-PTY localhost SSH. SystemPlaceCommands spawns an isolated local SSH process group, and capture_child on deadline kills/reaps that group (backend.rs:1979-2019,2268-2278); it does not remotely signal the Podman PID. OpenSSH V_9_6_P1 session.c:2483-2523 explicitly handles a channel dying before its child: absent a PTY it closes/detaches channel state without killing that child. systemd v255 run.c:1535-1721 moves the command through the transient scope job then execs it; that scope is not the local SSH client's group. Podman detached run creates/starts first (ABI containers.go:1129-1165); cmd containers/run.go:214-225 prints its ID only after the engine returns. A closed output pipe is therefore not an implicit pre-create cancellation. This is an already-running external process blocked on named filesystem work, not a Rust future resuming after helm death or an arbitrary scheduler pause.

After the remote command deadline the production prepare path attempts reconcile_helpers, whose normal libpod inspect cannot resolve this storage-only builder; its persisted recent pending name is retained (:630-675). There are no retired images yet (:41-45), so prepare_images returns the error (:267-289). environment_session_steps returns it (tensorlake_add.rs:521-539); finish_session_launch emits an error reply (:1028-1057), and the test's reply[error] assertion at podman_environments.rs:826-830 panics. Its catch boundary then stops/reaps the helm and runs fallback (:1276-1293). Fallback scans only visible recipe labels (:1217-1251), never the pending name/storage-only inventory. Its empty container/image checks can therefore succeed before the stalled remote operation completes; once it does, libpod registration/start can continue. This route uses an explicit handled command timeout followed by a reachable test assertion, not a conjectured 30-minute timeout during the early first run.

External primary sources checked: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/go.mod ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/storage/v1.51.0/store.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/common/v0.57.4/libimage/image.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/libpod/storage.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/libpod/runtime_ctr.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/libpod/container_commit.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/pkg/ps/ps.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/pkg/domain/infra/abi/containers.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v4.9.3/cmd/podman/containers/run.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/run/run.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openssh/openssh-portable/V_9_6_P1/session.c . Earlier web-rendered upstream line numbers stripped blank lines; the new citations here use raw numbered source.

No uninvestigated source branch remains for this stated conditional route. Unmeasured premises are occurrence/duration of the specified filesystem stall and actual installed engine/SSH versions, storage backend and configured wrappers; the test accepts a supported range and does not pin those host facts. Reading the same functions again cannot establish that an actual run experiences the stall. A version/config manifest or authorized observation could establish occurrence, but no reproduction or process/live-install operation is requested or performed. This is likely conditional source analysis, not a confirmed observed leak. The early confirmed wording and prior UAI details remain in append-only history; no original consequence or proposed-drop basis is erased.
